# Puffin Ship

> Puffin Ship is automated video production. Choose the type of video you want to make, upload your files, and answer a few questions, and Puffin Ship builds a project that makes the video. The project is a reusable video template: every video after the first uses the same style, with a new script or new footage, in about a minute of your time. It is for marketing teams, agencies, and creators, and the videos are made for LinkedIn, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube and websites.

## How it works

1. **Choose the type.** On the New project screen, pick the card closest to your idea, or pick "Something else" and describe it.
2. **Upload your files.** Recordings, screen captures, photos or clips from your phone, or files already in your workspace. Some types need no footage at all, such as an AI avatar reading your script. For a series, say you will add new files each time.
3. **Answer the questions.** A short chat asks only what it cannot choose well itself: vertical or landscape, roughly how long, who is on screen, which settings stay the same and which change every video, and where a video should stop for you to check (for example after the script is written). It builds a first draft while you answer.
4. **Reuse the style.** Your answers become a project, a reusable video template for that kind of video. Press New Video, add this time's script or footage, and the video comes out in the same style. Change the project once and every later video gets the change.

After a video is made you can edit one version (trim or move a clip, fix a caption) and carry the fix back to the project, download the MP4, subtitles and a Final Cut Pro project, and share a link others can comment on. Brand kits put your colors, fonts and logo on every video.

## Types of video

Talking-head short from a recording; short from a script you write; AI avatar presenter; product demo or walkthrough; tutorial for a tool or library; clips from a webinar, talk or podcast; stream or gameplay highlights; news or commentary series; story from your footage; founder or pitch video; explainer told in animated graphics; turn a blog post or article into a short; or something else, described in plain words.

## Showcase

The showcase features recent videos from the founder's own workspace, each made from a project and presented by his AI avatar: How to Buy a Snowboard; Is "fake snow" actually fake? (how snowmaking works); Why your phone dies at 30% on a ski lift; Maeklong Railway Market (a travel story cut from clips); and The science of deep frying a turkey, made from the same project as the snowboard video. It also keeps three more example shorts: a product tutorial made in Puffin Ship, plus a news explainer and an event interview made with the process Puffin Ship automates.

## Use with your AI agent

Puffin Ship works with any AI tool that supports MCP, the open standard for connecting AI apps to other services, including ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini CLI and VS Code. Add https://app.puffinship.com/mcp as an MCP server or connector, sign in and approve it, then ask for the video you want. The agent can start a new project with you, upload footage through a link, start a video once you agree, answer review stops as you decide, and hand you the MP4 and Final Cut Pro project. It asks before anything that costs money, and it never asks you to paste a key into the chat. Setup steps for each app: https://app.puffinship.com/docs/guides/mcp-connect.html

Developers can also start videos from their own systems through the API.

## Time saved

Editing a short by hand often takes over an hour: scrubbing the recording for the moment, then cropping, captioning, and cutting the pauses (editors commonly quote 30 to 60 minutes of editing per finished minute of video). With Puffin Ship the editing runs on its own, so the time per video is a few minutes to pick and review.

## Who's building it

Puffin Ship is built by Chandler Mayo (https://www.linkedin.com/in/chandlermayo). He has built software for more than a decade and spent the last seven years in developer relations at Redpanda, Doppler, and PubNub, making talks, videos, and technical content. Turning those recordings into shorts was always the slow part, so he built Puffin Ship to do it, and has been running it to make shorts for early teams. Puffin Ship, Inc. is the company behind it.

## Pricing

One plan, priced by usage in tokens, with no tiers and no seats. A token is one cent, and every version of a video shows the tokens it used, step by step. A typical 45 to 60 second short uses about 100 to 350 tokens, and one with a lot of cut-in footage or animated graphics up to about 800. New accounts start with $25 in credit (2,500 tokens, roughly 7 to 25 shorts). Nothing is charged automatically; more tokens are bought by contacting Puffin Ship. Avatars, voices, generated video and images, and stock footage use your own account with each service, connected with your own key, and that service bills you directly. Some restrictions apply (see the Terms of Service: https://app.puffinship.com/terms).

## Your footage

Customers keep ownership of everything they upload, and it is used to make their videos. Rated versions can also help improve Puffin Ship's models; that is on by default and a workspace admin can turn it off in workspace settings.

## Set up for you

Teams that would rather not set it up themselves can have the Puffin Ship team build their projects, fit it into how they already work, or run it for them. Ask through the form at https://puffinship.com/contact/
